newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian parliament to blast NATO, defend Lenin.
newsitem.headline: Russian parliament to blast NATO, defend Lenin.

text.p: The opposition-dominated lower house of parliament was to consider resolutions on Wednesday banning the burial of Lenin and ruling out Russia joining NATO.
The State Duma voted overwhelmingly to put both motions, proposed by the communist faction, on the agenda of its Wednesday session.

Russian opposition to NATO's plans to expand eastwards is expected to be the central issue of a summit in Helsinki between U.S. President Bill Clinton and Russia's Boris Yeltsin on Thursday and Friday.

Yeltsin and the communist-dominated opposition are united in fierce resistance to plans by the Western defence alliance to invite as members several former states of the defunct Soviet-led Warsaw Pact.
There have been no realistic moves to invite Russia to join NATO and the Duma resolution appeared aimed at trying to steal the limelight from Yeltsin.
The issue of Lenin, leader of the 1917 Bolshevik revolution and founder of the Soviet state, whose mummified body is on public display in a mausoleum on Red Square, is much more controversial.
Democrats say he should be buried according to Christian traditions and Yeltsin last week mentioned a possible referendum on the issue.
The opposition dismisses the idea fiercely, seeing Lenin's mausoleum as their sacred place of pilgrimage.
In a separate move, the Duma decided to invite Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin to address deputies on Friday over the new composition of the government.
Yeltsin reshuffled the government radically this week, giving key positions to youthful reformers including Anatoly Chubais, public enemy number one for the communists.

The Duma appears to be hesitating over its course of action. Some members are ready to work for a no-confidence vote in the government, which, if passed twice, would give Yeltsin a choice of dismissing either the cabinet or the legislature.
Others seem to be less radical and want to wait for the new cabinet to make its policy clear.
